The AJF variant of MAM for Sefaria

Author: Ben Denckla

Revision: 2026-10-26

Introduction

Beside its files for Sefaria, MAM-for-Sefaria has an AJF variant of them: the folder csv-ajf/, and the folder misc/unicode-names-ajf/, which lists its code points. This page describes the two. It tells them apart from the folders csv/ and misc/unicode-names/, which the pages The encoding of MAM for Sefaria and The Unicode-name listings of MAM for Sefaria describe. Every count and example on it is taken from the files.

This page has three typographic conventions:

  1. Text styled like this reveals more on hover, where the medium allows hovering.
  2. Text styled like this draws attention to letters of a form, as to the ב of אבג.
  3. ZARQA is the name of a Unicode code point, less the words that name its script and class. Hovering shows the whole name, here HEBREW ACCENT ZARQA.

The files

The folder csv-ajf/ has a file for each of the 39 books, named as the file of csv/ for that book is, as I Samuel.csv is, and a provenance note, _provenance.md. Each book's file is a CSV file in UTF-8, with CRLF line ends and no byte-order mark, as those of csv/ are, but it has no header. Each of its 23,213 rows is a verse, with four fields: the verse's reference, its text, and its cant-alef and cant-bet strands, which are empty but in the 24 verses that have two cantillations: Gen 35:22; Exod 20:2–6, 8–10 and 13–15; and Deut 5:6–10, 12–15 and 17–19.

In those verses the second field has the text that represents both strands, as csv/ has it too. The third and fourth fields have the strands themselves, which are, as the guide to MAM-simple's JSON says, the תחתון and עליון strands in the Decalogues, and the פשוטה and מדרשית strands at Gen 35:22.

The text is plain: it has no HTML, and neither of the two spaces that csv/ writes as character references. So the two folders spell some things differently:

csv/ csv-ajf/
a samekh break NO-BREAK SPACE, then {ס} in a span, then eight more SPACE, {ס}, SPACE
a pe break NO-BREAK SPACE, then {פ} in a span, then <br> SPACE, {פ}, SPACE
a legarmeh THIN SPACE, then PASEQ in <b> PASEQ, right after its atom
a paseq THIN SPACE, PASEQ in <small>, THIN SPACE two PASEQ marks, with no space on either side
a space of song spacing eight NO-BREAK SPACE characters SPACE
a ketiv and its qere in the order MAM has them the ketiv first
a trivial pair, an implicit maqaf, or a small, large or hung letter in a span or element of its own the text alone

In the text field of csv-ajf/, each of these has the count it has in csv/: 1,787 legarmeh and 508 paseq marks, 1,982 samekh and 1,571 pe breaks, and 1,047 pairs of a ketiv and its qere.

At each of the 2 atoms where MAM's source identifies a silluq with a meteg after it, the text field has the atom that csv/ has, without that meteg. The section A meteg after the silluq of The encoding of MAM for Sefaria shows them.

Verse numbering

The verses of csv-ajf/ are numbered as BHS numbers them, and those of csv/ as Sefaria numbers them, so a reference can name different text in the two folders. The page Versification Differences: MAM, BHS, and Sefaria lists the differences. Every reference of csv/ is also in csv-ajf/, which has 7 more: Exod 20:24–26, Num 25:19 and Deut 5:31–33.

As in csv/, the rows of Josh 21:36–37, for which MAM has no text, have only an EM DASH (—) as their text, and the files have no other EM DASH.

The listings

The folder misc/unicode-names-ajf/ has a listing for each file of csv-ajf/, named and written as those of misc/unicode-names/ are, which the page The Unicode-name listings of MAM for Sefaria describes, but for three things:

  1. The line that names a verse gives BHS's numbering, as Levit 1:1 in vtrad vtbhs does.
  2. The text has no HTML, so no line has START or STOP.
  3. A verse with two cantillations lists each of its three texts after a line that names it, rv-cant-combined, rv-cant-alef or rv-cant-bet, with the text's lines indented by four spaces.

In 9 of those verses, the listing's rv-cant-bet text ends with a SPACE line that the file lacks: the strand ends with a samekh break, and the writer of the CSV files strips spaces from the end of a row's last field, while the listings are written from the unstripped text.

These are all 90 code points that the text and strand fields of csv-ajf/ have, with the short name that each has in the listings, and how many times the fields have it:

Two strands on one letter

Every atom of csv/ that has a COMBINING GRAPHEME JOINER (CGJ) is in the text field of csv-ajf/ as often, and the strand fields have no CGJ. In the verses with two cantillations, 14 letters have a CGJ, and on each of them the marks before it are one strand's, and the marks after it the other's. Each strand field has that letter with its own marks alone, which the tables show in the attention color. They give each atom's references in both folders, since the two numberings differ in the Decalogues. In 4 atoms, one strand has a QAMATS and an accent or METEG below the letter, and the other a PATAH and an accent above it:
